name: antevemus/aspecification
description: Enterprise Specification Pattern Framework for PHP 8.2+ (DDD, Notification Pattern, SQL Query Visitor, Adianti TCriteria, DAG Repositories)

authors.name: Heliton Junior - CTO @ Antevemus Soluções Inovadoras em TI Ltda.

suggest.ext-pdo: PdoRepository (repository over PDO: specifications compiled to SQL, attribute or builder mapping), the PDO persistence of the state machine and the PDO domain-event outbox
suggest.antevemus/alinq-collection: ^2.2.0 — ALinqBridge (typed IALinqCollection/IALinqLazyCollection returns), ALinqSpecificationVisitor and lazy streaming over IRepository::iterate() (Module 14); requires PHP 8.4; reads a non-public property only when marked #[Specifiable], as this package does (2.x resolves properties through the same shared accessor, antevemus/adeep-property-access)
suggest.ext-intl: TextComparison::IgnoreCaseAndAccents and Spec::equalIgnoreCaseAndAccents(): text compared ignoring case and accents (Normalizer: NFD without the nonspacing marks); without it those specifications are refused when built (MissingExtensionException) and every other text operator keeps working
suggest.ext-curl: HttpDataSource: concurrent data resolution over HTTP through curl_multi (DataResolver, Module 21); without it an HttpDataSource is refused when registered and CallableDataSource keeps working
suggest.ext-sysvsem: SysVSemaphoreSynchronizer: read/write lock shared between processes through SysV IPC semaphores (SemaphoreSynchronizer is intra-process)
suggest.antevemus/aspecification-revolt: ^1.0 — RevoltDataSource and RevoltStageTransport: the non-HTTP sources of a resolution stage fetched concurrently under the Revolt event loop (Fibers, Amp futures) through the IDeferredDataSource/IStageTransport hook of 2.6.0
suggest.psr/simple-cache: ^1.0 || ^2.0 || ^3.0 — CachedRuleCatalog, CachedFeatureFlagStore and PartitionRepository::withIndexCache() (2.8.0): the rule catalog, the feature flags and the routing clusters of a partitioned repository read through a PSR-16 cache shared between servers, with an implementation of your choice (Redis, Memcached, APCu); without it those classes cannot be built and nothing else changes
